title: Projective-bundle morphisms are proper
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. If $f$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], meaning that $X$ is isomorphic over $S$ to a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)$ for a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal E$, then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), together with Lemma 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective) and Definition 01W8 (definition-projective).

proof.text: Unpack [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: write $P=\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ with projection $\pi:P\to S$, and choose a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ over $S$ with $f=\pi i$ (absorbing the given $S$-isomorphism into $i$). By the finite-type clause of [pqf-def-coherent], every point of $S$ has a neighbourhood $V$ carrying a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E|_V$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U\subseteq V$ of that point using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Restriction is still surjective: the local expressions for a section restrict to their intersections with $U$. The images of the standard basis are thus finitely many global sections of $\mathcal E|_U$ generating it in exactly the sense of [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. If $n=0$, use the single zero section instead. These $U$ cover $S$. Quasi-coherence and finite type of $\mathcal E|_U$ follow immediately from their local definitions in [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Tags 01W8(1) and 01WB, proof: choose affine neighbourhoods and finite generators; Modules Tags 01B5 and 01AM

proof.text: For each chosen $U$, identify $P_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ over $U$ with $\mathbf P_U(\mathcal E|_U)$. Here this is restriction of the defining gluing datum, not an assumption that the module is locally free. Indeed, for every affine open $W\subseteq U$, clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] identifies the section algebra in either construction with $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S(W)}(\mathcal E(W))$, sending the same section $e$ to its degree-one generator. These identifications preserve degrees: the degree-$m$ part is spanned by products of $m$ such generators [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Their restriction maps agree on coefficients and on degree-one generators, hence on all products and sums. Thus the local Proj schemes, their structure maps, their localized overlap maps, and their cocycles are the same in the two constructions of [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Restricting that gluing to the affine cover of $U$ gives the claimed identification, carrying $\pi|_{P_U}$ to the projective-bundle projection $\pi_U$. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01WB, proof: restriction of the projective bundle to an affine neighbourhood; Constructions Tag 01OB and definition-relative-proj

proof.text: The module $\mathcal E|_U$ is finite type and quasi-coherent and is generated by the finite family in Step 1. Therefore [lem-trf-projective-bundle-global-generated-h-projective] applies over $U$ and makes $\pi_U:\mathbf P_U(\mathcal E|_U)\to U$ H-projective. Apply [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], whose projectivity convention is precisely the finite-projective-space convention, to conclude that $\pi_U$ is proper. Under the over-$U$ identification in Step 2 this is properness of $\pi|_{P_U}$: the separated, finite-type and universally-closed conditions defining properness are unchanged by an isomorphism over the base [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tags 01WB and 01WC, proofs: local finite-projective-space embedding followed by properness; the globally generated embedding is also the indicated paragraph of Tag 087S

proof.text: Put $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$. The restriction $i_U:X_U\to P_U$ is the base change of $i$ along the open immersion $P_U\hookrightarrow P$, and is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. To check the source, $i(x)$ lies in $P_U$ exactly when $\pi i(x)=f(x)$ lies in $U$; equivalently the pullback of the open subscheme $P_U$ along $i$ is the open subscheme $f^{-1}(U)$. The restriction of $f$ is $\pi|_{P_U}\circ i_U$, because $f=\pi i$. Step 3 gives that $P_U$ is proper over $U$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] now says that this composite is proper. Thus every $X_U\to U$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 01WC, proof, closed-immersion and composition sentence; Tags 01QR, 01W5 and 01W3

proof.text: The opens $U$ in Step 1 cover $S$, and Step 4 proves properness of every restriction $f^{-1}(U)\to U$. Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] to this cover. Its conclusion is that $f$ is proper, as required. The cover may be infinite, and properness is only asserted globally after applying this target-locality theorem.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01WB and 01WC, proofs, with the finite-type definition 01B5 and the globally generated projective-bundle embedding of 087S
